items.stem: Which term matches this description: "An instrument used to work out latitude by measuring the height of the Sun or a star above the horizon"?
items.answer: astrolabe
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of astrolabe.

items.stem: Explain the difference between the voyages of Vasco da Gama and the voyages of Zheng He.
items.answer: Zheng He's huge Ming fleets (1405–1433) displayed Chinese power and collected tribute but were then stopped; da Gama's small fleet (1497–1499) sought trade and led to Portuguese forts and a long-lasting commercial empire in the Indian Ocean.
items.markingKey: Zheng He's huge Ming fleets (1405–1433) displayed Chinese power and collected tribute but were then stopped; da Gama's small fleet (1497–1499) sought trade and led to Portuguese forts and a long-lasting commercial empire in the Indian Ocean. items.stem: Rafael writes: "Europeans discovered empty lands." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: The Americas, Africa and Asia were home to millions of people with their own states and societies; "discovery" reflects a European perspective.
items.markingKey: The Americas, Africa and Asia were home to millions of people with their own states and societies; "discovery" reflects a European perspective. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.answer: It investigates causation (geography, technology, royal sponsorship) over a clear period with available sources.

items.stem:
Source A – Ship's journal (paraphrased): Paraphrase of the journal of Christopher Columbus, October 1492, surviving in a later summary by Bartolomé de las Casas

The admiral wrote that the people he met were gentle and generous and would easily become Christians. He added that with fifty men they could all be kept under control and made to do whatever was wanted, and that he hoped to find where the gold they wore came from.

Explain one value and one limitation of Source A for an investigation into the motives and voyages of European exploration, referring to its origin and purpose.
items.answer: Origin: Paraphrase of the journal of Christopher Columbus, October 1492, surviving in a later summary by Bartolomé de las Casas. Purpose: to report to the Spanish monarchs on the voyage and encourage further support. Value: It is an early record of first contact and shows Columbus's aims – conversion, control and gold. Limitation: It survives only in a later copy and summary, and Columbus wrote to impress his sponsors; it gives no Taíno perspective.
items.markingKey: Origin: Paraphrase of the journal of Christopher Columbus, October 1492, surviving in a later summary by Bartolomé de las Casas. items.stem: ""Gold" was the most important motive for European exploration." To what extent is this view justified?
items.answer: Economic gain was the strongest motive overall, but it was intertwined with religious and political aims that rulers used to justify expeditions.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: the spice trade and gold promised huge profits; merchants and investors funded voyages for profit. Arguments against: spreading Christianity was a sincere motive for rulers like Isabella; national rivalry and personal fame (glory) drove kings and captains. Supported judgement: Economic gain was the strongest motive overall, but it was intertwined with religious and political aims that rulers used to justify expeditions. The historian argued that the most important results of Columbus's voyages were biological rather than political: the transfer of plants, animals and germs between hemispheres reshaped diets, landscapes and populations across the world more than any treaty or battle.

items.stem: Briefly explain why the Columbian Exchange changed environments in the Americas.
items.answer: Introduced cattle, pigs, sheep and horses grazed and spread across the land, Old World weeds and crops replaced native vegetation, and plantations cleared forests.

items.stem: Explain why European diseases killed so many Indigenous Americans.
items.answer: Indigenous Americans had never been exposed to Old World diseases such as smallpox and measles, so they had no immunity; epidemics spread ahead of colonists, and war, famine and forced labour made people more vulnerable.

items.answer: Abolishing the trade (Britain 1807, USA 1808) stopped the buying and shipping of new captives; abolishing slavery (British colonies from 1834, USA 1865, Brazil 1888) freed people who were already enslaved.

items.stem: Write the introduction and an outline of the body paragraphs for an essay that evaluates the view that "The actions of enslaved people were the most important reason for the abolition of slavery."
items.answer: Thesis: A strong argument: resistance was central, but abolition came from the interaction of resistance, campaigns and economic and political change.

items.answer: Origin: Paraphrase of Olaudah Equiano, "The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano", London, 1789. Purpose: to describe his life and to persuade British readers to support the abolition of the slave trade. Value: It is a rare first-hand account by someone who experienced enslavement, and it shows how abolitionists used personal testimony. Limitation: It was written decades after the events for a campaign; some historians have debated where Equiano was born, although the conditions he describes are confirmed by many other sources.

items.answer: Campaigns by abolitionists (including formerly enslaved people such as Equiano), petitions, boycotts of slave-grown sugar, fear of revolts after Haiti and changing economic interests combined to persuade Parliament.

items.stem: Jonas writes: "British rule began in India in 1600." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: 1600 is the date of the Company's charter as a trader; territorial rule began after Plassey (1757) and the diwani (1765).

items.answer: It gave the Company the land revenue of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, so it could pay for its armies and buy Indian goods with Indian taxes – turning a trading company into a ruling power.

items.stem: Briefly describe the Battle of Plassey (1757) and explain what it reveals about how the Company gained power.

The author argued that India was being impoverished because a large part of its revenue was sent to Britain each year as salaries, pensions, interest and profits, without any equivalent return. He called this a continuous "drain" of India's wealth.

items.answer: Origin: Paraphrase of Dadabhai Naoroji, "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India", London, 1901. options: A sudden, widespread outbreak of an infectious disease
The period from the 15th to the 17th century when European states sent expeditions across the oceans
Sailing all the way around the world
The right to collect land revenue, granted to the EIC in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa by the Mughal emperor in 1765
items.answer: A sudden, widespread outbreak of an infectious disease
items.markingKey: A. "epidemic" is a sudden, widespread outbreak of an infectious disease.

items.stem: Define the term "resistance".
items.answer: Actions taken by enslaved people to oppose slavery, from running away and sabotage to revolts
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: actions taken by enslaved people to oppose slavery, from running away and sabotage to revolts. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "Age of Exploration".
items.answer: The period from the 15th to the 17th century when European states sent expeditions across the oceans
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the period from the 15th to the 17th century when European states sent expeditions across the oceans. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain the difference between a zamindar under the Permanent Settlement and a ryot under the ryotwari system.
items.answer: Under the Permanent Settlement, zamindars were made landowners responsible for paying a fixed revenue; under the ryotwari system (Madras, Bombay) peasants (ryots) paid revenue directly to the state.
items.markingKey: Under the Permanent Settlement, zamindars were made landowners responsible for paying a fixed revenue; under the ryotwari system (Madras, Bombay) peasants (ryots) paid revenue directly to the state. items.stem: "The Columbian Exchange only moved goods from Europe to the Americas." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Exchange went in both directions and involved Africa and Asia too – American crops spread across the world.
items.markingKey: Exchange went in both directions and involved Africa and Asia too – American crops spread across the world. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly explain why European traders turned to enslaved African labour in the Americas.
items.answer: Plantations of sugar, tobacco and later cotton needed huge, cheap labour forces; Indigenous populations had collapsed from disease, and European traders could buy captives from some African states in exchange for goods.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Plantations of sugar, tobacco and later cotton needed huge, cheap labour forces; Indigenous populations had collapsed from disease, and European traders could buy captives from some African states in exchange for goods. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why the Treaty of Tordesillas mattered for later history.
items.answer: It gave Portugal lands east of the line, including Brazil and the route to Asia, and Spain most of the Americas, which is why Brazil speaks Portuguese and most of Latin America Spanish; other powers ignored it.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: It gave Portugal lands east of the line, including Brazil and the route to Asia, and Spain most of the Americas, which is why Brazil speaks Portuguese and most of Latin America Spanish; other powers ignored it. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why the doctrine of lapse created resentment among Indian rulers.
items.answer: It let the Company annex states such as Jhansi and Satara when a ruler had no natural son, ignoring the Indian custom of adoption, so rulers feared losing their lands.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: It let the Company annex states such as Jhansi and Satara when a ruler had no natural son, ignoring the Indian custom of adoption, so rulers feared losing their lands. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why American crops led to population growth in parts of Europe, Africa and Asia.
items.answer: Potatoes, maize and sweet potatoes produce many calories per hectare and grow in poor soils, so they increased food supplies – e.g. the potato in Ireland and northern Europe and maize in Africa and China.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Potatoes, maize and sweet potatoes produce many calories per hectare and grow in poor soils, so they increased food supplies – e.g. the potato in Ireland and northern Europe and maize in Africa and China. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Nia is investigating the Atlantic slave trade: its causes, experiences and abolition and proposes the research question: "Why was slavery bad?" Explain one weakness of this research question and write a more focused alternative.
items.answer: Weakness: it is a closed moral question whose answer is obvious; it does not investigate evidence Improved: "How did the testimony of formerly enslaved people contribute to the British campaign to abolish the slave trade between 1787 and 1807?"
items.markingKey: 1 mark: weakness identified (it is a closed moral question whose answer is obvious; it does not investigate evidence); 1-2 marks: a focused question such as "How did the testimony of formerly enslaved people contribute to the British campaign to abolish the slave trade between 1787 and 1807?" (clear scope – place, period or group – and open, researchable wording); 1 mark: justification of the change. items.stem: Rio de Janeiro lies at about 43°W and Moscow at about 38°E. Using local solar time (the Sun crosses 15° of longitude per hour), if it is 14:00 local solar time in Rio de Janeiro, what is the local solar time in Moscow?
items.answer: 19:24 (Moscow is 5 h 24 min ahead)
items.markingKey: Longitude difference 81° (M1); ÷ 15 = 5.40 h = 5 h 24 min (A1); Moscow is east so ahead → 19:24 (A1). Official time zones differ from solar time.

items.answer: British rule drained India's wealth to Britain, causing poverty.

items.stem: Tariq argues that "The Columbian Exchange did more harm than good." Ana disagrees. Explain one piece of evidence each student could use, and state which view you find more convincing and why.
items.answer: For the peoples of the Americas and Africa it was overwhelmingly harmful; its benefits were real but spread unequally and mainly later.
items.markingKey: Tariq: disease caused the deaths of tens of millions of Indigenous people. Ana: new crops improved diets and allowed population growth across the world. items.stem: According to US census, the number of enslaved people in the United States changed from 697,897 people (1790) to 3,953,760 people (1860). Calculate (a) the percentage change and (b) the average change in people per year.
items.answer: (a) +466.5%; (b) +46,512.33 people per year

items.stem: Two places lie on the same line of longitude, one at 50°S and the other at 55°N. Given that 1° of latitude is about 111 km, estimate the distance between them.
items.answer: about 11,655 km
items.markingKey: Difference in latitude = 105° (crossing the equator adds both values) (M1); × 111 km = 11,655 km (A1).

items.stem: Outline two points that could be used to evaluate the claim: "The Columbian Exchange did more harm than good."

items.answer: A strong argument: resistance was central, but abolition came from the interaction of resistance, campaigns and economic and political change.

items.stem: You have three weeks to investigate "Why did Portugal, rather than Spain, reach India by sea first, between 1415 and 1498?" Outline a step-by-step plan, the sources you would use and one way you would evaluate your process at the end.

items.stem: "The East India Company ruled India mainly in the interests of its shareholders." To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: Largely true: profit and revenue drove policy, although Parliamentary control and local collaboration modified it over time.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: revenue and trade profits were its main aims, as the 1770 famine showed; policies such as the Permanent Settlement maximised fixed revenue. items.stem: Which of the following best describes "abolition"?

The right to collect land revenue, granted to the EIC in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa by the Mughal emperor in 1765
A very large and rapid fall in population
An English trading company chartered in 1600 that became the ruler of much of India by the 19th century
items.answer: The ending of the slave trade or of slavery itself by law

items.stem: Explain the difference between a negative impact of the Columbian Exchange and a positive impact of the Columbian Exchange.
